     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
    77	  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0

+# Independent adversarial review: 61-correct-bracketing
+
+The candidate contains a successful and non-vacuous proof of an **internal loop
+theorem**, but it does not contain a reachability claim that loads, calls, or
+otherwise pins the submitted `solution.mpy`. A materially wrong replacement of
+the real function leaves the submitted proof unchanged and still produces
+`#Top`. This is a real-program adequacy failure, not a K infrastructure failure.
+
+Audit environment: K v7.1.337, Python 3.10.12, supplied-semantics mode. All
+execution used fresh source copies under `/tmp/audit-work`; no candidate
+definition, cache, trace, or compiled artifact was reused.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+### Trusted-mount consistency
+
+The rendered mode is `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`, and
+`/reference/reference-semantics` is present. There is no mode/mount
+contradiction, so this is a candidate audit rather than `AUDIT_ERROR`.
+
+The recursive, no-symlink comparison found that
+`/candidate/reference-semantics` and the trusted tree have exactly the same
+entries, entry types, and bytes. `diff -r --no-dereference` exited 0. Both trees
+contain one root K file plus 23 files below `semantics/`, all regular files, and
+no candidate semantics symlink. The candidate prompt and translator are also
+byte-identical to the trusted mounts:
+
+- `prompt.py`: SHA-256
+  `f900fc0b3f9f9e3d6380108cad345c8211f454cac5496d16402442819340e1bb`
+- `py2mpy.py`: SHA-256
+  `406485eac118431c08ef59f30f79dfa6aa9d5825408917fc5ce7c806e664db16`
+
+Commands, manifests, hashes, exit statuses, and missing-file checks are in
+[`evidence/stage1-integrity.log`](evidence/stage1-integrity.log), generated by
+[`evidence/stage1_integrity.sh`](evidence/stage1_integrity.sh).
+
+### Missing provenance artifacts
+
+The following requested candidate artifacts are absent, not symlinks or
+mistyped entries:
+
+- `/candidate/run-input.json`
+- `/candidate/metrics.json`
+- `/candidate/codex-last.txt`
+- `/candidate/codex-output.log`
+
+`/candidate/PROOF.md` is also absent. Therefore there is no generation metadata
+or final proof report to corroborate. This is a candidate provenance/evidence
+defect; it did not prevent independent reconstruction.
+
+The extra `/candidate/__pycache__/solution.cpython-310.pyc` was ignored as a
+candidate-built cache. `/candidate/kore-exec.tar.gz` was inspected only as
+untrusted evidence and never executed. It contains `spec.kore`,
+`vdefinition.kore`, a shell command, and logs. Its log actually records
+`WarnStuckClaimState` followed by `ErrorException`, not `#Top`. This historical
+trace has no bearing on the fresh proof result. Bounded inspection is preserved
+in [`evidence/stage1-untrusted-trace.log`](evidence/stage1-untrusted-trace.log)
+and the inspection script in
+[`evidence/stage1_untrusted_trace.sh`](evidence/stage1_untrusted_trace.sh).
+
+Stage 1 result: semantics, prompt, and translator integrity pass; requested
+provenance records are missing.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Contract
+
+On the promised domain, `brackets` is a string containing only `(` and `)`.
+The canonical behavior is:
+
+1. the running number of opens minus closes must never be negative; and
+2. the final number must be zero.
+
+Equivalently, every prefix contains at least as many `(` as `)`, and the whole
+string contains equal counts. This explains why a premature close such as
+`")(()"` is false even if later characters might increase the balance.
+
+The generated Python uses the same algorithm as the canonical function. Its
+extra `bracket = ""` initialization has no observable effect. On each
+character, `(` increments `balance`, every other character decrements it, a
+negative balance returns false immediately, and exhaustion returns
+`balance == 0`.
+
+### Translation identity
+
+Running the trusted translator on the copied `/candidate/solution.py` produced
+a file byte-identical to the submitted `solution.mpy`; both have SHA-256
+`9022bba7a15313c42602d1d5dc7f84072698d274da99fa12267e5ada75508e51`.
+The exact command and exit status are in
+[`evidence/stage2-fidelity.log`](evidence/stage2-fidelity.log).
+
+### Independent differential test
+
+[`evidence/differential_test.py`](evidence/differential_test.py) independently
+imports `/reference/canonical.py` and the copied generated entry point. It
+tested:
+
+- all four documented examples;
+- 13 explicit empty, one-character, unbalanced, nested, sequential, and
+  long-boundary cases;
+- all 8,191 parenthesis strings of lengths 0 through 12; and
+- 416 deterministic generated strings at lengths 13–17, 31–33, 63–65, and
+  127–128.
+
+After deduplication, 8,610 inputs were compared with zero mismatches. The exact
+input manifest is
+[`evidence/differential-inputs.json`](evidence/differential-inputs.json), and
+the command/result is in
+[`evidence/stage2-fidelity.log`](evidence/stage2-fidelity.log). This is strong
+finite implementation-fidelity evidence, not a substitute for a K theorem.
+
+Stage 2 result: program fidelity passes on the intended domain.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+Only source files were copied to `/tmp/audit-work/candidate-src`. Candidate
+caches, the bytecode file, and the KORE archive were not used. Fresh output
+directories were created below `/tmp/audit-work/build`.
+
+The concrete definition was rebuilt with:
+
+```text
+kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k --backend llvm \
+  --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition /tmp/audit-work/build/runtime-kompiled
+```
+
+It exited 0. The proof definition was rebuilt with:
+
+```text
+kompile verification.k --backend haskell \
+  --main-module VERIFICATION --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition /tmp/audit-work/build/verification-kompiled
+```
+
+It also exited 0. The build emitted fixed-semantics warnings about
+non-exhaustive `[total]` functions (`mapStrVS`, `floorFI`, `toF`, `ceilF`,
+`joinCodes`, and `valSeqAt`) plus unused variables. None of those functions
+occurs on this program's proof path.
+
+The exhaustive inventory found exactly one candidate positive reachability
+claim, label `loop`. It was independently run with:
+
+```text
+kprove spec.k \
+  --definition /tmp/audit-work/build/verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SPEC --claims loop
+```
+
+It exited 0 and printed `#Top`. Full bounded outputs and statuses are:
+
+- [`evidence/stage3-runtime-build.log`](evidence/stage3-runtime-build.log)
+- [`evidence/stage3-proof-build.log`](evidence/stage3-proof-build.log)
+- [`evidence/stage3-claim-loop.log`](evidence/stage3-claim-loop.log)
+- [`evidence/stage3-reconstruction.log`](evidence/stage3-reconstruction.log)
+
+Stage 3 result: the only submitted claim reconstructs successfully. There is no
+positive entry-point claim to reconstruct.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### What the submitted claim says
+
+The claim at `/candidate/spec.k:10` starts in an already active function frame.
+In plain language, its precondition is:
+
+- `<k>` begins with the exact internal `#loop` for remaining string codes `S`,
+  followed by the source's final `return balance == 0` and `#endcall`;
+- local frame 1 already exists and contains `balance = B`, a string-valued old
+  `bracket`, and a string-valued `brackets`;
+- the current environment is frame 1, the caller is frame 0, and the stack
+  contains the corresponding return frame;
+- return and exception cells are clear, the exit code is zero, and
+  `B >= 0`; and
+- the heap, heap counter, globals, continuation, old loop-variable value, and
+  original input codes are otherwise symbolic.
+
+Its postcondition says that the frame has been popped, caller state restored,
+and the Boolean term `correctCodes(S, B)` placed immediately before the saved
+continuation. Heap and heap counter are preserved. This is result-constraining:
+the result is not a fresh variable, tautology, or one-way implication.
+
+The proof-local function at `/candidate/verification.k:10` defines
+`correctCodes` structurally. Empty input tests `B == 0`; code 40 (ASCII `(`)
+increments; every other code returns false at balance zero or decrements a
+positive balance. Under `B >= 0`, this exactly describes the source loop.
+
+A concrete satisfying state is:
+
+```text
+B=0, S=.IntSeq, OLD=str(.IntSeq), INPUT=.IntSeq,
+GLOBALS=.Map, HEAP=.Map, HLOC=0, CONT=.K
+```
+
+with the fixed cells shown in the claim. Eight ground substitutions, including
+empty input, `"("`, `"()"`, `")"`, and positive-balance internal states, agreed
+between `correctCodes`, the canonical Python function, and the generated Python
+function. Evidence is in
+[`evidence/stage4-adequacy.log`](evidence/stage4-adequacy.log), produced by
+[`evidence/claim_witnesses.py`](evidence/claim_witnesses.py).
+
+Fresh LLVM execution of the exact copied source plus 12 assertions over normal
+and boundary inputs ended with `.K`, `NoExc`, and exit code 0. The generated
+configuration retains the real `correct_bracketing` closure and exact submitted
+body. This confirms that the supplied semantics can execute the program, but it
+does not add a theorem to the candidate. See
+[`evidence/stage4-adequacy.log`](evidence/stage4-adequacy.log).
+
+### Missing real-program connection
+
+The claim does **not** execute the submitted program. Neither `spec.k` nor
+`verification.k` contains `solution.mpy`, `correct_bracketing`, `Module(...)`,
+`Call(...)`, or `#loadAll`. Their dependency chain is only:
+
+```text
+spec.k -> verification.k -> reference-semantics/semantics.k
+```
+
+The claim begins after all of these unproved operations:
+
+- module loading and registration of the actual function body;
+- lookup and call of `correct_bracketing`;
+- parameter binding of the concrete input;
+- `balance = 0`;
+- `bracket = ""`; and
+- evaluation of `Name("brackets")` into the iterator used by `#loop`.
+
+It also never requires `S == INPUT`; `INPUT` is explicitly reported unused by
+the compiler. The comment claiming that the public entry case is “its `B = 0`
+instance after the two initialization assignments” is an informal assertion,
+not a submitted reachability theorem.
+
+The reviewer-authored body-sensitivity test makes the gap concrete. It inserted
+an unconditional `return True` before the original body, regenerated a
+byte-different MPY, and exhibited `"("` as a satisfying intended-domain input:
+the canonical result is false and the mutated result is true. With no proof
+artifact changed, the submitted `loop` claim still exited 0 and printed
+`#Top`. Commands and outputs are in
+[`evidence/stage5-body-sensitivity.log`](evidence/stage5-body-sensitivity.log);
+the mutation generators are
+[`evidence/make_body_mutation.py`](evidence/make_body_mutation.py) and
+[`evidence/body_mutation_check.py`](evidence/body_mutation_check.py).
+
+Stage 4 result: **FAIL**. The internal theorem is sound and result-constraining,
+but it does not pin the real generated program.
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Exhaustive inventory
+
+[`evidence/rule_inventory.py`](evidence/rule_inventory.py) emitted every
+top-level configuration, syntax declaration, context, rule, claim, module,
+import, and require block with its full source, line number, hash, and
+attributes. The complete 218,932-byte inventory is
+[`evidence/rule-inventory.txt`](evidence/rule-inventory.txt); its generation
+command and hash are in
+[`evidence/stage5-inventory-command.log`](evidence/stage5-inventory-command.log).
+
+It contains 228 syntax declarations, 697 rules, five contexts, one
+configuration, and one claim. Among the declarations/rules are 147
+`[function]`, 108 `[total]`, 45 priority, 26 `owise`, 36 `concrete`, 25
+`symbol`, and 22 `no-evaluators` classifications. There are no
+`[functional]`, `[simplification]`, or literal `[opaque]` attributes.
+
+The rule disposition by file is below. “Fixed baseline” means the source is
+byte-identical to the supplied semantics selected by the problem; every
+individual item in that file is enumerated in the inventory. The used-path
+rules were additionally traced rule by rule below. Unused fixed-baseline
+modules have no matching redex on this program or claim and introduce no
+candidate-local shortcut.
+
+| File | Syntax | Rules | Disposition |
+|---|---:|---:|---|

+| `bool.k` | 0 | 13 | Fixed baseline; truthiness/Boolean equality |
+| `builtins.k` | 38 | 137 | Fixed baseline; unused by proof path |
+| `call.k` | 3 | 21 | Fixed baseline; required by the missing entry path |
+| `comprehension.k` | 3 | 7 | Fixed baseline; unused |

+
+Every construct in `solution.mpy` has a fixed declaration and rule path:
+
+- `Module` and statement sequencing: `syntax.k:56-61`,
+  `core.k:49-60`, and `core.k:124-127`.
+- `FuncDef`/`Params`: `syntax.k:53-60` and `functions.k:14-16`.
+- `Name`, `Int`, `Bool`, and `Str`: `syntax.k:9-13`,
+  `core.k:131-154`, `core.k:194-196`, and `str.k:13-17`.

+  `controls.k:9-31`.

+  in `tuple.k:31-35`.
+- `If`: `syntax.k:49` and `controls.k:51-54`.
+- `Compare`/`CmpOp`: `syntax.k:30-32`, evaluation contexts and dispatch

+For the internal claim, evaluation is left-to-right where relevant: the loop
+binds one string character, string equality selects the increment/decrement
+branch, the integer update writes `balance`, the negative test either performs
+an abrupt `Return(false)` that pops the frame or continues to the residual

+claim's cells exactly cover the state read or changed by that region:

+heap counter, exception, and exit code are preserved.
+
+### Candidate-local proof extension
+
+`correctCodes(IntSeq, Int)` is a definitional result summary, not an
+operational bridge:
+
+- Its two rules cover the disjoint `.IntSeq` and `iCons` constructors.
+- The cons rule covers every integer code and balance.
+- Guards are internal Boolean conditionals, so there is no rule overlap.
+- Recursion strictly decreases the `IntSeq`.
+- For the claim's complete domain `B >= 0`, the equations agree with the fixed
+  loop step, early-return behavior, and final equality.
+- The same opaque symbol is not injected into execution. The universal loop
+  claim executes fixed semantics and establishes the connection to the
+  function, so this is not a circular oracle bridge.
+
+There are no candidate-local priority rules, semantic rewrites,
+simplifications, opaque primitives, or body-bypassing call rules. I do not
+label either candidate-local rule unsound; consequently there is no alleged
+unsound-rule false-conclusion witness to supply. The rejection is the narrower
+and independently witnessed absence of an entry theorem.
+
+### Fixed-semantics totals and opaque symbols
+
+The imported supplied semantics contains opaque or proof-total boundaries,
+fully listed here even though none is reached by this claim:
+
+- `sortVS`, `sortKeyVS`, and `md5hexCodes`;
+- `intFloatDiv`, `divII`, `floatMod`, `floatLt`, `absF`, `subF`, `divF`,
+  `addF`, `mulF`, `powF`, `gtF`, `eqF`, `decStrToF`,
+  `divFloatIntV`, `intToF`, `truncF`, `roundF`, `roundFN`, and `sqrtF`;

+`mapStrVS`, `joinCodes`, and the three conversion functions above. These are
+fixed supplied-semantics trust boundaries and are irrelevant to the
+parenthesis-string claim: no term headed by any of them appears in its
+execution or destination.

+Stage 5 result: the internal proof rules are sound, but the full static review
+confirms there is no rule or claim connecting them to the submitted program
+entry.
+
+## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test
+
+The candidate supplied no `spec-vacuity.k`. The reviewer-authored mutation is
+[`evidence/spec-vacuity.k`](evidence/spec-vacuity.k). It changes the
+result-constraining destination from:
+
+```text
+correctCodes(S, B)
+```
+
+to:
+
+```text
+notBool (correctCodes(S, B))
+```
+
+This is demonstrably false for the satisfying ground input
+`S=.IntSeq, B=0`: the loop and original destination are true, while the mutated
+destination is false.
+
+`kprove --dry-run` exited 0, proving that the mutation parsed and built against
+the fresh definition. The real proof exited 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState`; its

+timeout, missing import, or unrelated crash.
+
+Exact commands, statuses, and residuals are in:
+
+- [`evidence/stage6-mutation-dry-run.log`](evidence/stage6-mutation-dry-run.log)
+- [`evidence/stage6-mutation-proof.log`](evidence/stage6-mutation-proof.log)
+- [`evidence/stage6-nonvacuity.log`](evidence/stage6-nonvacuity.log)

+repair real-program pinning.
+

+### Formally established
+
+Conditional on the supplied K semantics and K toolchain, the successful
+reachability proof establishes this partial-correctness statement:
+
+> For every remaining code sequence `S` and every nonnegative balance `B`, if
+> execution starts at the exact submitted internal `#loop` state and reaches
+> the specified return configuration, it returns `correctCodes(S, B)`, restores
+> the caller/frame cells stated in the claim, and preserves the framed cells.
+
+The claim is universal over `S`, `B`, continuation, globals, old loop variable,
+input field, heap, and heap counter. Its false-result mutation confirms that
+the returned Boolean matters.
+
+It does **not** establish:
+
+- that `solution.mpy` is loaded;
+- that `correct_bracketing` resolves to the submitted body;
+- that a call binds the public input to frame 1;
+- that the two initialization assignments reach `B=0`;
+- that the loop iterator `S` is the called input;
+- or the public theorem `correct_bracketing(brackets) == correctCodes(codes,

+

+1. **K implementation and built-in domains.** K v7.1.337, its Haskell/LLVM
+   backends, and the imported `INT`, `BOOL`, `STRING`, `MAP`, `LIST`,

+2. **Supplied MPY semantics.** The byte-identical
+   `/reference/reference-semantics` is the fixed language model selected by the

+   theorem, the relevant subset models unbounded integers, ASCII parentheses,
+   deterministic string iteration, scope writes, loop control, return, and

# Independent adversarial review: 61-correct-bracketing

The candidate contains a successful and non-vacuous proof of an **internal loop
theorem**, but it does not contain a reachability claim that loads, calls, or
otherwise pins the submitted `solution.mpy`. A materially wrong replacement of
the real function leaves the submitted proof unchanged and still produces
`#Top`. This is a real-program adequacy failure, not a K infrastructure failure.

Audit environment: K v7.1.337, Python 3.10.12, supplied-semantics mode. All
execution used fresh source copies under `/tmp/audit-work`; no candidate
definition, cache, trace, or compiled artifact was reused.

## 1. Input and provenance integrity

### Trusted-mount consistency

The rendered mode is `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`, and
`/reference/reference-semantics` is present. There is no mode/mount
contradiction, so this is a candidate audit rather than `AUDIT_ERROR`.

The recursive, no-symlink comparison found that
`/candidate/reference-semantics` and the trusted tree have exactly the same
entries, entry types, and bytes. `diff -r --no-dereference` exited 0. Both trees
contain one root K file plus 23 files below `semantics/`, all regular files, and
no candidate semantics symlink. The candidate prompt and translator are also
byte-identical to the trusted mounts:

- `prompt.py`: SHA-256
  `f900fc0b3f9f9e3d6380108cad345c8211f454cac5496d16402442819340e1bb`
- `py2mpy.py`: SHA-256
  `406485eac118431c08ef59f30f79dfa6aa9d5825408917fc5ce7c806e664db16`

Commands, manifests, hashes, exit statuses, and missing-file checks are in
[`evidence/stage1-integrity.log`](evidence/stage1-integrity.log), generated by
[`evidence/stage1_integrity.sh`](evidence/stage1_integrity.sh).

### Missing provenance artifacts

The following requested candidate artifacts are absent, not symlinks or
mistyped entries:

- `/candidate/run-input.json`
- `/candidate/metrics.json`
- `/candidate/codex-last.txt`
- `/candidate/codex-output.log`

`/candidate/PROOF.md` is also absent. Therefore there is no generation metadata
or final proof report to corroborate. This is a candidate provenance/evidence
defect; it did not prevent independent reconstruction.

The extra `/candidate/__pycache__/solution.cpython-310.pyc` was ignored as a
candidate-built cache. `/candidate/kore-exec.tar.gz` was inspected only as
untrusted evidence and never executed. It contains `spec.kore`,
`vdefinition.kore`, a shell command, and logs. Its log actually records
`WarnStuckClaimState` followed by `ErrorException`, not `#Top`. This historical
trace has no bearing on the fresh proof result. Bounded inspection is preserved
in [`evidence/stage1-untrusted-trace.log`](evidence/stage1-untrusted-trace.log)
and the inspection script in
[`evidence/stage1_untrusted_trace.sh`](evidence/stage1_untrusted_trace.sh).

Stage 1 result: semantics, prompt, and translator integrity pass; requested
provenance records are missing.

## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks

### Contract

On the promised domain, `brackets` is a string containing only `(` and `)`.
The canonical behavior is:

1. the running number of opens minus closes must never be negative; and
2. the final number must be zero.

Equivalently, every prefix contains at least as many `(` as `)`, and the whole
string contains equal counts. This explains why a premature close such as
`")(()"` is false even if later characters might increase the balance.

The generated Python uses the same algorithm as the canonical function. Its
extra `bracket = ""` initialization has no observable effect. On each
character, `(` increments `balance`, every other character decrements it, a
negative balance returns false immediately, and exhaustion returns
`balance == 0`.

### Translation identity

Running the trusted translator on the copied `/candidate/solution.py` produced
a file byte-identical to the submitted `solution.mpy`; both have SHA-256
`9022bba7a15313c42602d1d5dc7f84072698d274da99fa12267e5ada75508e51`.
The exact command and exit status are in
[`evidence/stage2-fidelity.log`](evidence/stage2-fidelity.log).

### Independent differential test

[`evidence/differential_test.py`](evidence/differential_test.py) independently
imports `/reference/canonical.py` and the copied generated entry point. It
tested:

- all four documented examples;
- 13 explicit empty, one-character, unbalanced, nested, sequential, and
  long-boundary cases;
- all 8,191 parenthesis strings of lengths 0 through 12; and
- 416 deterministic generated strings at lengths 13–17, 31–33, 63–65, and
  127–128.

After deduplication, 8,610 inputs were compared with zero mismatches. The exact
input manifest is
[`evidence/differential-inputs.json`](evidence/differential-inputs.json), and
the command/result is in
[`evidence/stage2-fidelity.log`](evidence/stage2-fidelity.log). This is strong
finite implementation-fidelity evidence, not a substitute for a K theorem.

Stage 2 result: program fidelity passes on the intended domain.

## 3. Clean proof reconstruction

Only source files were copied to `/tmp/audit-work/candidate-src`. Candidate
caches, the bytecode file, and the KORE archive were not used. Fresh output
directories were created below `/tmp/audit-work/build`.

The concrete definition was rebuilt with:

```text
kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k --backend llvm \
  --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
  --output-definition /tmp/audit-work/build/runtime-kompiled
```

It exited 0. The proof definition was rebuilt with:

```text
kompile verification.k --backend haskell \
  --main-module VERIFICATION --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
  --output-definition /tmp/audit-work/build/verification-kompiled
```

It also exited 0. The build emitted fixed-semantics warnings about
non-exhaustive `[total]` functions (`mapStrVS`, `floorFI`, `toF`, `ceilF`,
`joinCodes`, and `valSeqAt`) plus unused variables. None of those functions
occurs on this program's proof path.

The exhaustive inventory found exactly one candidate positive reachability
claim, label `loop`. It was independently run with:

```text
kprove spec.k \
  --definition /tmp/audit-work/build/verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module SPEC --claims loop
```

It exited 0 and printed `#Top`. Full bounded outputs and statuses are:

- [`evidence/stage3-runtime-build.log`](evidence/stage3-runtime-build.log)
- [`evidence/stage3-proof-build.log`](evidence/stage3-proof-build.log)
- [`evidence/stage3-claim-loop.log`](evidence/stage3-claim-loop.log)
- [`evidence/stage3-reconstruction.log`](evidence/stage3-reconstruction.log)

Stage 3 result: the only submitted claim reconstructs successfully. There is no
positive entry-point claim to reconstruct.

## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning

### What the submitted claim says

The claim at `/candidate/spec.k:10` starts in an already active function frame.
In plain language, its precondition is:

- `<k>` begins with the exact internal `#loop` for remaining string codes `S`,
  followed by the source's final `return balance == 0` and `#endcall`;
- local frame 1 already exists and contains `balance = B`, a string-valued old
  `bracket`, and a string-valued `brackets`;
- the current environment is frame 1, the caller is frame 0, and the stack
  contains the corresponding return frame;
- return and exception cells are clear, the exit code is zero, and
  `B >= 0`; and
- the heap, heap counter, globals, continuation, old loop-variable value, and
  original input codes are otherwise symbolic.

Its postcondition says that the frame has been popped, caller state restored,
and the Boolean term `correctCodes(S, B)` placed immediately before the saved
continuation. Heap and heap counter are preserved. This is result-constraining:
the result is not a fresh variable, tautology, or one-way implication.

The proof-local function at `/candidate/verification.k:10` defines
`correctCodes` structurally. Empty input tests `B == 0`; code 40 (ASCII `(`)
increments; every other code returns false at balance zero or decrements a
positive balance. Under `B >= 0`, this exactly describes the source loop.

A concrete satisfying state is:

```text
B=0, S=.IntSeq, OLD=str(.IntSeq), INPUT=.IntSeq,
GLOBALS=.Map, HEAP=.Map, HLOC=0, CONT=.K
```

with the fixed cells shown in the claim. Eight ground substitutions, including
empty input, `"("`, `"()"`, `")"`, and positive-balance internal states, agreed
between `correctCodes`, the canonical Python function, and the generated Python
function. Evidence is in
[`evidence/stage4-adequacy.log`](evidence/stage4-adequacy.log), produced by
[`evidence/claim_witnesses.py`](evidence/claim_witnesses.py).

Fresh LLVM execution of the exact copied source plus 12 assertions over normal
and boundary inputs ended with `.K`, `NoExc`, and exit code 0. The generated
configuration retains the real `correct_bracketing` closure and exact submitted
body. This confirms that the supplied semantics can execute the program, but it
does not add a theorem to the candidate. See
[`evidence/stage4-adequacy.log`](evidence/stage4-adequacy.log).

### Missing real-program connection

The claim does **not** execute the submitted program. Neither `spec.k` nor
`verification.k` contains `solution.mpy`, `correct_bracketing`, `Module(...)`,
`Call(...)`, or `#loadAll`. Their dependency chain is only:

```text
spec.k -> verification.k -> reference-semantics/semantics.k
```

The claim begins after all of these unproved operations:

- module loading and registration of the actual function body;
- lookup and call of `correct_bracketing`;
- parameter binding of the concrete input;
- `balance = 0`;
- `bracket = ""`; and
- evaluation of `Name("brackets")` into the iterator used by `#loop`.

It also never requires `S == INPUT`; `INPUT` is explicitly reported unused by
the compiler. The comment claiming that the public entry case is “its `B = 0`
instance after the two initialization assignments” is an informal assertion,
not a submitted reachability theorem.

The reviewer-authored body-sensitivity test makes the gap concrete. It inserted
an unconditional `return True` before the original body, regenerated a
byte-different MPY, and exhibited `"("` as a satisfying intended-domain input:
the canonical result is false and the mutated result is true. With no proof
artifact changed, the submitted `loop` claim still exited 0 and printed
`#Top`. Commands and outputs are in
[`evidence/stage5-body-sensitivity.log`](evidence/stage5-body-sensitivity.log);
the mutation generators are
[`evidence/make_body_mutation.py`](evidence/make_body_mutation.py) and
[`evidence/body_mutation_check.py`](evidence/body_mutation_check.py).

Stage 4 result: **FAIL**. The internal theorem is sound and result-constraining,
but it does not pin the real generated program.

## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review

### Exhaustive inventory

[`evidence/rule_inventory.py`](evidence/rule_inventory.py) emitted every
top-level configuration, syntax declaration, context, rule, claim, module,
import, and require block with its full source, line number, hash, and
attributes. The complete 218,932-byte inventory is
[`evidence/rule-inventory.txt`](evidence/rule-inventory.txt); its generation
command and hash are in

individual item in that file is enumerated in the inventory. The used-path
rules were additionally traced rule by rule below. Unused fixed-baseline

## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test

The candidate supplied no `spec-vacuity.k`. The reviewer-authored mutation is
[`evidence/spec-vacuity.k`](evidence/spec-vacuity.k). It changes the
result-constraining destination from:

```text

```

to:

```text

```

This is demonstrably false for the satisfying ground input
`S=.IntSeq, B=0`: the loop and original destination are true, while the mutated
destination is false.

`kprove --dry-run` exited 0, proving that the mutation parsed and built against
the fresh definition. The real proof exited 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState`; its
residual explicitly requires `B == 0` to equal `notBool (B == 0)` on the empty

timeout, missing import, or unrelated crash.

Exact commands, statuses, and residuals are in:

- [`evidence/stage6-mutation-dry-run.log`](evidence/stage6-mutation-dry-run.log)
- [`evidence/stage6-mutation-proof.log`](evidence/stage6-mutation-proof.log)
- [`evidence/stage6-nonvacuity.log`](evidence/stage6-nonvacuity.log)

### Formally established

Conditional on the supplied K semantics and K toolchain, the successful
reachability proof establishes this partial-correctness statement:

> For every remaining code sequence `S` and every nonnegative balance `B`, if
> execution starts at the exact submitted internal `#loop` state and reaches

- that `solution.mpy` is loaded;
- that `correct_bracketing` resolves to the submitted body;
- that a call binds the public input to frame 1;
- that the two initialization assignments reach `B=0`;
- that the loop iterator `S` is the called input;
- or the public theorem `correct_bracketing(brackets) == correctCodes(codes,

   backends, and the imported `INT`, `BOOL`, `STRING`, `MAP`, `LIST`,
   `K-EQUAL`, and related hooks are trusted. They affect all machine-checking.
   This is the normal low-level proof-tool boundary.
2. **Supplied MPY semantics.** The byte-identical
   `/reference/reference-semantics` is the fixed language model selected by the
   task. The complete inventory records every declaration and rule. For this
   theorem, the relevant subset models unbounded integers, ASCII parentheses,
   deterministic string iteration, scope writes, loop control, return, and
   frame popping. This is acceptable for the intended input domain.
3. **Unused opaque/total primitives.** Every such symbol is listed in Stage 5.
   They are imported but do not influence control, state, result, or
   postcondition here. Their presence is therefore acceptable but not evidence
   about other programs.
4. **Trusted translator.** `/reference/py2mpy.py` is trusted as the Python-to-MPY
   bridge. Byte identity proves that the submitted MPY is exactly what that
   translator emits for the candidate source; it does not prove translator
   correctness in general.
5. **`correctCodes` mathematics.** Its recursive equations are
   reviewer-audited ordinary mathematics, and the K loop claim universally
   connects the fixed internal execution to them. The additional bridge from
   `correctCodes(S,0)` to the English bracketing property is an informal
   induction, supported but not proved by the differential data.
6. **Python and concrete-execution evidence.** The 8,610-case differential
   test, 12 K smoke assertions, and eight claim substitutions are empirical
   bridges only. They support implementation/intent alignment over the tested
   values and do not replace the reachability proof.
7. **Missing entry bridge.** The candidate informally assumes that the internal
   claim is reached from the real function call after initialization. This
   boundary is illegitimate for the requested theorem because it is exactly
   the program-pinning obligation. The wrong-body witness shows that the proof
   is insensitive to the submitted body.

### Final decision

The fresh `#Top` and failed false-result mutation make the internal loop lemma
credible. Nevertheless, a proof of that detached state is not a proof of the
real generated program. The absence of any entry claim, together with the
successful proof after a materially wrong body mutation, meets the decision
rule for a substituted/unpinned program.

LEGITIMACY: NOT_LEGIT
